elements.evidence: 2.11 ... 'extend to Corio's affiliates (any entity controlling, controlled by or under common control with Corio)'

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: 2.11 ... 'and to contractors acting on Corio's behalf'
2.2 is 'fully paid up, perpetual', but 2.3 is only a 'royalty-free, fully paid up right and license' with no perpetual term
only the fee-bearing 2.1 grant is 'perpetual and irrevocable'; the paid-up grants in 2.2 and 2.3 contain no irrevocability language

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: no termination standard for any subscription/hosting licence appears in the rendered text; only 14.1 assignment and the Section 2 grants are present
14.1 permits assignment in an M&A or asset sale 'except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required'
2.11 extends all Section 2 licences to affiliates outright, which exceeds the notice-conditioned fallback

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: 14.1 'either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets ... without such consent'

reasons: The inserted 2.11 cleanly achieves the affiliate and contractor limbs of the preferred position and is a concise insertion for an otherwise absent concept, so minimality is satisfied.

Preferred is not fully achieved: the paid-up grants in 2.2 and 2.3 are not expressly irrevocable (2.3 is not even perpetual), no 'terminable only for uncured material breach' standard was added for the subscription/hosting licence, and 14.1 transferability is still cut back by the direct-competitor consent carve-out.

The clause nonetheless sits at (indeed above) the fallback: affiliates are covered without a notice condition and successor transfer in an M&A transaction is permitted, so the result is acceptable rather than a deviation.
No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics are introduced; Sections 2.1-2.4, 2.10 and 14.1 remain fully effective.
